g.text: Kubernetes KMS v2 & k8s-kms-plugin Figure %page% of %lastpage%
Kubernetes KMS API v2 - k8s.io/kms/apis/v2 & KMS Plugin for PKCS #11
CKA_ID (Byte array) PKCS #11 Key identifier for public/private key pairs
DEK Data Encryption Key (derived by kube-apiserver from the 32-byte DEK seed)
EncryptResponse.Ciphertext holds a JWE for the aes-gcm / aes-cbc / rsa-oaep families,
and a 60-byte binary envelope (nonce | AES-GCM(DEK seed) | tag) for ml-kem.
kem-ciphertext.k8s-kms-plugin.keysealer.eclipse.org for ml-kem only. They are stored
in plaintext in etcd and handed back verbatim on the matching DecryptRequest.
KeyId is the hex-encoded CKA_ID of the KEK.
KMS v2 & Kubernetes first startup & Status heartbeet
run k8s-kms-plugin serve with a KEK stored on the TPM or HSM
at startup and cache it ; indefinite
KMS v2 first Encrypts DEK Seed
wrap the DEK seed with the remote KEK
return wrapped DEK seed & KEK ID,
KeyId:<hex CKA_ID of the KEK as string>,
on the ML-KEM key pair found by CKA_ID / CKA_LABEL
return (KEM ciphertext c, shared secret K)
c: 768/1088/1568 B ; K: 32 B transient session key
derive an AES key from K with KMAC (NIST SP 800-185),
then AES-GCM-seal the DEK seed under it
(K and the derived key are zeroed afterwards)
KeyId:<hex CKA_ID of the KEK as string>,
The KEM ciphertext c cannot travel in Ciphertext: KMS v2 caps it at 1 kB and c is up to
1568 B. It is carried in a plaintext annotation instead, which is safe because c is
key-establishment material only (ML-KEM is IND-CCA2; tampering fails the AES-GCM tag check).
[every minute when plugin is healthy or every 10 seconds when the plugin is not healthy]
